mechanism_narrative: Continued weakness in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT will keep discretionary trips suppressed, so RETAIL_REC stays below its prior four-week average over the next month. The mechanism is that fewer commuting-linked trips reduce incidental shopping and dining visits.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remains negative and TRANSIT remains deeply negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean for four consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover materially from current levels.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES stays depressed, people substitute home-based activity for out-of-home shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. The causal claim is that home anchoring directly crowds out discretionary retail visits.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 while WORKPLACES stays below -30
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is above baseline and WORKPLACES is below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the previous four weeks after RESIDENTIAL exceeds +10 and WORKPLACES remains below -30 for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below its already depressed level marks tightening mobility frictions; retail visitation then falls with a one-week lag because fewer people can combine errands with trips outside home. This predicts lower RETAIL_REC only when transit access deteriorates again.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from the current level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already near -62 in the snapshot
failure_condition: A week after a new TRANSIT decline of more than 5 points, RETAIL_REC is not lower than the prior week or the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: An uptick in PARKS after a very negative week signals substitution toward outdoor leisure, which diverts time and spending away from retail outlets for the next two to four weeks. The effect should be visible only if the park rebound is sustained rather than a one-week spike.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises from below 0 to above +5 and stays positive for two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -19.3 to +12.0 and then back negative
failure_condition: After a two-week positive PARKS spell, RETAIL_REC is not below its last-four-week average within the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays positive while RETAIL_REC keeps falling, households are concentrating trips on essentials and cutting discretionary shopping. That essential-only pattern should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 for four consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC is below -15
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stays positive or near zero while RETAIL_REC trends downward in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean despite four weeks of positive GROCERY_PHARM and current RETAIL_REC below -15.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from the current trough by more than 10 points, the commuting channel will re-open and retail activity will improve within four weeks. The claim fails when workplace recovery does not translate into more retail visitation.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 points from the current weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -58.1 to -33.0 over the snapshot
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 points but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean over the following four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL indicates weather- or holiday-driven home and outdoor substitution, which lowers shopping-center visits over the next one to two weeks. The retail drop is strongest when both proxies move in the same direction.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is elevated while PARKS is volatile in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after both PARKS and RESIDENTIAL rise together.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed improvement in TRANSIT combined with a slowdown in the recent WORKPLACES decline would signal broader foot-traffic recovery, raising RETAIL_REC over the next month. The mechanism fails if transit improves but workplace mobility stays deeply negative.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 8 points from its current level while WORKPLACES stays above -40
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is very low and WORKPLACES has partially recovered from its trough
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by at least 8 points and WORKPLACES stays above -40, yet RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-four-week mean over the next four weeks.
